references.text: The requirement that the sacrificial animal must be without blemish is repeated here, specifying that cattle must be a male without defect to be accepted by the Lord.
The introduction to the laws concerning the peace offering (זֶבַח־שְׁלָמִים), which describes the basis for the sacrifice mentioned in Leviticus 22:21.
The peace offering from the small livestock must also be without blemish, whether male or female, emphasizing the requirement of perfection.
The immediate context describing the requirements for burnt offerings from vows and freewill offerings, where the animal must be without defect to be accepted.
Refers to an offering to the Lord from cattle or small livestock, either as a vow or a freewill offering, parallel to Leviticus 22:21.
Reiterates the prohibition against sacrificing animals with defects, such as lameness or blindness, to the Lord your God.
Forbids offering cattle or small livestock with defects to the Lord, as it is an abomination.
The prophet Malachi rebukes the people for bringing blind, lame, and sick animals as sacrifices, contrary to the requirement of unblemished animals.
Condemnation of one who promises a male from the flock but offers a defective animal to the Lord.
Christ is compared to an unblemished lamb (ἀμώμου), fulfilling the requirement of perfection in the sacrifice from the Old Testament.
Christ offered himself without blemish (ἄμωμον) to God, as the perfect sacrifice that fulfills the law of offerings.
